result.summary: Gated TEST-DESIGNER's commit 7ad9a8a against all 8 checks; all PASS. (1) Coverage: read test/letflow/api/pagination_test.exs and test/specs/REQ-067.md directly (not TEST-DESIGNER's own report) -- confirmed every one of REQ-067's six ACs has runnable, passing, non-skipped tests: AC1 constants (4 tests, lines 18-32), AC2 page-size reject-not-clamp incl. non-numeric/0/201 boundaries (11 tests, lines 38-84), AC3 cross-endpoint prefix rejection (3 tests, lines 90-108), AC4 expiry incl. deliberately-old-timestamp and custom-window (3 tests, lines 114-138), AC5/INV-1 tenant isolation (2 tests, lines 144-199), AC6 pagination completeness across 3 pages (2 tests, lines 205-277). (2) Grepped test file and spec for 'TODO'/'@tag :skip'/'skip' -- zero matches in either file. (3) Fixtures checked: fixture_rows/0, fixture_list/2 (INV-1), fixture_all_items/0, fixture_page/3 (AC6) are private functions returning fresh literal data per call, no module attribute or shared process state, no cross-test coupling. (4) Every test builds all its own inputs locally (raw cursor strings, fixture lists); AC6's 3 sequential page calls happen inside one test, not across tests -- no execution-order dependency confirmed by re-running with ExUnit's own seed (987921, non-sequential by default since async: true). (5) Grepped for password/secret/connection-string patterns in both files -- zero matches; confirmed explicitly N/A, this module makes no Ecto.Repo or Plug.Conn call (moduledoc states this and the module source has no such calls). (6) INV-1 non-tautology, reasoned through directly: two tests exist. Test 'Cursor's struct fields are exactly [:inner]' (line 144) is the one that actually catches the named hypothetical regression -- if Cursor grew a :tenant field, Map.from_struct/1 |> Map.keys() would return more than one atom and the equality assertion against the literal [:inner] would fail outright, regardless of field order or whether any code path populates it. The second test (tenant-A-minted cursor replayed scoped to tenant B, line 174) is fixture-only: fixture_list/2 pattern-matches only %Cursor{inner: inner} and explicitly ignores inner's content (`_ = inner`), so on its own this test would pass even if Cursor gained extra fields (Elixir struct pattern matching on a named field doesn't fail when the struct has other fields) -- it demonstrates the concept (there is nothing in `inner` to misuse) but does not itself gate the regression. Verdict: the pair is not tautological because the struct-fields test is dispositive and would genuinely fail under the stated hypothetical; confirmed TEST-DESIGNER's own claimed second-assertion reasoning (tenant-A lookup on the same cursor, line 197) is real code, not asserted-only -- it does prove fixture_list isn't vacuously-empty, exactly as claimed. (7) Both self-reported bugs spot-checked as genuinely fixed in the committed file: stale-2024-timestamp bug -- the round-trip test (line 288) uses System.system_time(:microsecond), not a fixed past literal; colon-index bug -- the AC6 pager helper (line 220) calls Pagination.find_nth_colon(inner, 2) with an explanatory comment, not the wrong nth=1. Neither bug is present as an unfixed comment-only artifact. (8) Independently ran `mix test test/letflow/api/pagination_test.exs` (PATH: /c/Program Files/Elixir/bin) -- Result: 38 passed, 0 failed, 0.1s. Matches TEST-DESIGNER's reported count exactly.
